memory_lessons.applicability: Use the 8192-input direct-final candidate as a measured comparison point when testing alternative large-path finalization.
memory_lessons.claim: The four recorded T2 programs were valid and correct; the 8192-input direct-final candidate measured 9.062 μs versus 10.131 μs for 4096 inputs. These observations do not guarantee further improvement or establish a general tile-size trend.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the memset-plus-atomic candidate with the 8192-input direct-final candidate using full-domain correctness and total-run timings.

proposal.hypothesis: Keep the existing 128-thread CTA reduction, using 8192 inputs per CTA (512 first-stage CTAs at n=4194304), but replace scratch partials plus the final reduction CTA with an output memset followed by per-CTA atomic additions. This tests whether eliminating final partial reads and reduction work outweighs zero-fill cost and contention. The same-stream operations explicitly initialize output for every call; no inter-block ordering is assumed. Leave the small-n path unchanged.

retained: For n > 32768, increase each CTA's input tile to 8192 while retaining the existing 128-thread shared-memory reduction.
Initialize out with cudaMemsetAsync, then atomically add each first-stage CTA sum directly to out, replacing scratch partial writes and the final reduction CTA.
Leave the n <= 32768 reduction and copy path unchanged.
